about: GE-010-002 — the Tenure landing zone as a model, with every resource the AWS inventory records placed against a node of it. Nothing here has been applied: no AWS Organization exists. Guarded by tests/architecture/ge-landing-zone-model.test.mjs.

organization.evidence: docs/architecture/aws-inventory.json — organization.inUse is false, and access.denied records organizations:describe-organization, list-accounts and list-roots all refused. A single-account estate.
organization.creation_is_blocked_by: ADR-0007 — four operator decisions: which account becomes the management account, the consolidated-billing arrangement, root email addresses and tax/contact details for member accounts, and the disposition of the account currently running the live pilot.

nodes.name: Management
nodes.purpose: The account the Organization is created from. Runs nothing: no workload, no pipeline, no application data. Root has MFA, no routine access keys and no day-to-day use, because it is the only account with nothing above it.
nodes.existence_evidence: no Organization exists, so no management account exists either — aws-inventory.json organization.inUse=false

nodes.name: Security
nodes.purpose: Delegated security administration — GuardDuty, Config and Security Hub, administered from here rather than from the management account.

nodes.name: Log Archive
nodes.purpose: Write-once organization trail and Config history. The account whose contents an incident is reconstructed from, and which the accounts under investigation cannot edit.

nodes.name: Infrastructure
nodes.purpose: Shared build, artifact and registry estate, DNS and certificates. Terraform state and its lock table belong here: they describe every other account and are not owned by any one of them.

nodes.name: Tenure Parent
nodes.purpose: The global distribution engine — this repository and the System Studio. Its own OU rather than part of Infrastructure because it provisions and can destroy tenant infrastructure, and an account that can do that should not carry a shared build account's trust relationships.

nodes.name: Nonproduction
nodes.purpose: Development and staging cells. Roles here must be unable to reach production resources, which is GE-010-006 and is not provable in a single-account estate.

nodes.name: Production Cells
nodes.purpose: Pooled and bridge tenants, one account per cell. The live pilot's workload is a pooled production tenant and belongs to a cell here.

nodes.name: Dedicated Tenants
nodes.purpose: One Tenure-owned account per siloed or dedicated tenant, vended for them. A tenant is never asked for an AWS account, so the isolation boundary is one Tenure controls and can be accountable for.

nodes.name: Quarantine
nodes.purpose: Detached, deny-all. Where an account goes when it is compromised or being offboarded. Exists from day one and empty, because the time to discover that a deny-all OU does not exist is not during an incident.

nodes_with_nothing_to_place_today.why: This is a finding, not an omission. The inventory records no backup vault, no KMS alias, no WAF, no hosted zone and no nonproduction workload of any kind, and every resource it does record belongs to either the pilot or the Studio. Five of the nine nodes therefore have nothing to reconcile — the estate has no security-tooling account, no log archive and no nonproduction environment to move.

placements.undecided_reason: A service-linked role AWS creates in whichever account runs ECS, not a workload that moves. It will exist in every account that ends up running a task, so placing it against one node would be a false statement about a real resource. Settled by the same operator decision as the account itself — ADR-0007.
